properties.name: Niger Delta
properties.summary: Africa's largest wetland delta where the Niger meets the Atlantic — Nigeria's petroleum heartland.
properties.description: The delta covers roughly 70,000 km² of mangrove, freshwater swamp and barrier islands. It holds the bulk of Nigeria's oil and gas, a dense creek network, and highly politicised environmental and federal-revenue issues. Belt boundaries are approximate.
properties.elevationNote: Mostly near sea level; tidal mangrove
properties.character: Mangrove, oilfields, riverine settlements, barrier islands.
properties.economy: Oil and gas, fisheries, boat transport, refining and oil-palm agroforestry.
properties.agriculture: Hydromorphic gleysols, peat and alluvial deposits on seasonally flooded flats, backswamps and levees. Oil-palm agroforest dominates the better-drained levee ridges; fisheries are economically vital.
properties.crops: ["Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) — heart of the smallholder oil-palm belt","Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) — drier ridge plantations","Plantain and banana — staple on levee soils","Cassava — garri, lafun and fufu processing","Yam — white and yellow yam in the drier northern fringe","Rice — lowland swamp and fadama paddies","Cocoyam — shade-tolerant tuber under palm canopy","Fluted pumpkin (ugu) — widely intercropped leaf vegetable","Vegetables: amaranth, okra, peppers, garden egg","Coconut palm — barrier beaches and island fringes","Mangrove (Rhizophora, Avicennia) — fuelwood, poles and fisheries habitat","Fish, shrimp and crab artisanal fisheries — Nigeria's richest coastal fishery"]
properties.planting: ["Plant cassava and yam on levee ridges (higher drained ground) away from deep backswamps","Oil palms are usually retained on family farms — propagate by seedling and suckers at 9×9 m spacing","Use mounds and raised beds for vegetables in perennially waterlogged backswamp soils","Construct small fish ponds (earthen ponds) in abandoned rice fields for tilapia and catfish","Avoid draining mangrove wetlands — nursery habitat for fish stocks and shoreline protection"]

properties.name: Guinea Savanna
properties.summary: Wooded savanna belt between southern rainforest and northern Sudan/Sahel savanna.
properties.description: Guinea savanna (southern and northern Guinea) is Nigeria's broad middle belt: shea, yam, sorghum, and cattle routes. Rainfall is typically 900–1,500 mm. It includes much of Kwara, Niger, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa, and parts of Kaduna and FCT.
properties.character: Parkland trees, seasonal burn, mixed farming.
properties.economy: Yam, shea, grains, livestock corridors, Abuja hinterland.
properties.agriculture: Deep ferric luvisols support root crops and cereals. Shea parklands are retained on farm fields across the belt. Short fallow rotations are common.
properties.crops: ["Yam (Dioscorea rotundata) — white guinea yam is the staple tuber crop","Cassava (Manihot esculenta) — processed into garri, fufu, and flour","Guinea corn / Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) — guinea-corn for ogi, pap, and tuwo","Millet (Pennisetum glaucum) — early-maturing dry-season staple","Maize (Zea mays) — grown as second crop in yam/cassava rotations","Rice (Oryza sativa & O. glaberrima) — lowland fadama and upland varieties","Shea nut (Vitellaria paradoxa) — shea butter extraction, parkland agroforestry","Groundnut / Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) — oilseed and snack crop","Soybean (Glycine max) — expanding for oil and poultry feed","Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) — beans and leaves as vegetable","Sesame (Sesamum indicum) — northern guinea fringe for oilseeds","Mango, citrus, and cashew — scattered commercial orchards"]
properties.planting: ["Plant yam mounds (heaps) with stakes from November–December; seed yam setts planted February–April","Sorghum and millet sown at first rains (April–May); late maize July–August","Cassava stem cuttings planted March–May, harvested 9–18 months later","Shea trees retained as permanent parkland — do not clear mature shea on new farms","Use minimum tillage and tied ridges to reduce runoff on sloping ground"]

properties.name: Sudan Savanna
properties.summary: Open-tree savanna of the far-north fringe — drier than Guinea, main cereal and legume zone.
properties.description: Sudan savanna is Nigeria's northern crop-and-livestock belt with 500–900 mm annual rainfall, a shorter wet season (3–5 months) and scattered acacia and baobab trees. It covers most of Kano, Katsina, southern Sokoto, southern Borno, Jigawa, Bauchi and Gombe. Belt boundaries are approximate.
properties.elevationNote: Mostly 350–700 m undulating plains with inselbergs
properties.character: Acacia parkland, baobab, seasonal wadis, transhumance cattle corridors.

properties.name: Sahel Savanna
properties.type: Semi-arid vegetation belt at the desert fringe
properties.summary: Semi-arid grass and acacia steppe on the northern desert boundary — pastoral and resilient dry-crop zone.
properties.description: The Sahel is the narrow northernmost vegetation zone along the Niger border with under 500 mm annual rainfall and frequent droughts. It is dominated by short grass, sparse acacia and a pastoral economy of cattle, sheep and goats, with Lake Chad and the Komadugu–Yobe basins sustaining irrigation oases. Belt boundaries are approximate.
properties.elevationNote: 250–450 m; flat to gently rolling sandy plains
properties.character: Short annual grass, scattered thorny trees, wadis, transhumance routes and lake oases.
properties.economy: Pastoralism, drought-millet, lake-basin irrigation and gum-arabic agroforestry.
properties.agriculture: Very fragile sandy soils with low water-holding capacity — depend on drought-tolerant crops, water-harvesting structures and lake/fadama irrigation. Desertification and wind erosion are active challenges.
properties.crops: ["Drought millet (extra-early 60-day varieties)","Sorghum (early-maturing drought types)","Cowpea (drought-tolerant black-eyed varieties)","Wheat (Lake Chad pump irrigation)","Dryland rice (on fadamas where water is available)","Date palm (Lake Chad oases)","Gum arabic (Acacia senegal)","Balanites aegyptiaca (desert date)","Acacia nilotica","Wild melon / egusi-type gourds","Roselle (zobo)","Fodder sorghum–sudangrass hybrids"]
properties.planting: ["Plant millet as early as possible once rains establish (late June) — delay causes crop failure in short rainy seasons","Use zaï / tassa pits and half-moons to concentrate scarce runoff water around planting holes","Integrate livestock into crop rotation — penning animals on fields overnight builds soil fertility (korji / dung manuring)","Plant gum arabic (A. senegal) windbreaks across farm fields to reduce wind erosion and diversify income","Rely on indigenous drought-tolerant varieties — avoid hybrids requiring reliable water"]
properties.highlights: ["Northern pastoral zone","Lake Chad oases","Gum arabic belt"]

properties.name: Oban Hills
properties.summary: Cross River rainforest highlands linked to the Oban sector of Cross River National Park.
properties.description: The Oban Hills lie in the Cross River–Cameroon biodiversity hotspot with lowland and montane rainforest, drill monkeys and rare forest elephants. The terrain is rugged and heavily forested, and the belt is a sub-state highland within Cross River's rainforest. Belt boundaries are approximate.
properties.character: Rainforest, biodiversity hotspot, protected areas.
properties.economy: Ecotourism, conservation and limited hill farming.

properties.economy: Coconut, oil palm, swamp rice and coastal fisheries.

properties.name: Montane / Plateau
properties.summary: Nigeria's cool highlands — Irish potato, temperate vegetables and highland grains.
properties.description: Cool highland plateau and montane grassland/forest rising above the surrounding savanna — chiefly the Jos Plateau and the Mambilla highlands. Cooler temperatures and high orographic rainfall allow temperate crops that cannot be grown on the surrounding plains. Belt boundaries are approximate and patchy — it is an island belt, not a continuous zone.
properties.rainfall: 1,400–4,000 mm/yr on the highlands; 5–20°C (FAO montane/plateau climate)
properties.crops: ["Irish potato (Plateau)","Highland maize and beans","Temperate vegetables (cabbage, carrot, tomato)","Wheat (irrigated)","Pear and apple (Jos Plateau)"]
properties.agriculture: Volcanic and basement-complex soils on plateau surfaces; the cool climate supports temperate root and vegetable crops alongside highland cereals.
properties.economy: Irish potato (Plateau supplies roughly 90% of national output), temperate vegetables and highland grains.

properties.summary: Nigeria's historic tree-crop export, grown in shaded lowland rainforest.
properties.leadingNote: Ondo is Nigeria's largest cocoa-producing state; the south-west accounts for roughly three-quarters of national output.
properties.sources: [{"label":"ICCO — Feasibility Study on an Africa Cocoa Exchange, Nigeria annex","url":"https://www.icco.org/wp-content/uploads/4-FEASIBILITY-STUDY-ON-AFRICA-COCOA-EXCHANGE__Annex_NIGERIA.pdf"}]
properties.name: Cocoa

properties.summary: Nigeria's leading tuber staple, concentrated in the Middle Belt and forest fringe.
properties.leadingNote: Benue is the largest yam-producing state; Zaki Biam hosts Nigeria's biggest yam market.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Dubawa — Does Nigeria have the biggest yam market in the world? (FDC data)","url":"https://dubawa.org/does-nigeria-have-the-biggest-yam-market-in-the-world/"}]
properties.name: Yam

properties.summary: Coastal estate crop, led by the Lagos–Badagry belt.
properties.leadingNote: Lagos produces about 70% of Nigeria's coconuts, mainly from the Badagry belt.
properties.sources: [{"label":"The Guardian Nigeria — Lagos and the coconut connection","url":"https://guardian.ng/opinion/lagos-and-the-coconut-connection/"},{"label":"Blueprint — RMRDC and coconut production (1995 national coconut survey LGAs)","url":"https://blueprint.ng/rmrdc-saving-nigeria-n20bn-through-increased-coconut-production/"},{"label":"FAO — Lagos State coconut value chain study","url":"https://www.fao.org/sustainable-food-value-chains/library/details/en/c/1759734/"}]
properties.name: Coconut

properties.summary: Staple cereal grown on fadama and lowland paddies, with major producing hubs in the north-west and south-east.
properties.leadingNote: Kebbi is described as the hub of Nigerian rice production; Ebonyi's Abakaliki rice is a well-known brand.
properties.sources: [{"label":"The Guardian Nigeria — Nigeria can generate over $15bn from rice export (Bagudu)","url":"https://guardian.ng/features/nigeria-can-generate-over-15b-from-rice-export-yearly-bagudu/"}]
properties.name: Rice

properties.summary: Dry-season irrigated bulb crop of the north-west, dominated by Sokoto.
properties.leadingNote: Sokoto produced about 840,000 of Nigeria's ~2.1 million tonnes of onions in 2025 (about 40%), the largest share.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Blueprint — Governor Aliyu's onion revolution in Sokoto State (NOPPMAN)","url":"https://blueprint.ng/governor-aliyus-onion-revolution-in-sokoto-state/"}]
properties.name: Onion

properties.summary: Cool-climate tuber grown almost entirely on the Jos Plateau.
properties.leadingNote: Plateau accounts for about 90% of Nigeria's Irish potato production.
properties.sources: [{"label":"AfDB-assisted Potato Value Chain Support Project — Plateau share of output (via PotatoPro)","url":"https://www.potatopro.com/news/2025/bumper-potato-harvest-nigeria-drives-down-prices-attracts-buyers-across-africa"}]
properties.name: Irish Potato

properties.summary: Nigeria's largest food crop by area — garri, fufu, and starch for industry.
properties.leadingNote: Benue and the south-east/south-south belts dominate national cassava output; Nigeria is the world's largest producer.
properties.sources: [{"label":"FAO — Cassava production statistics","url":"https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL"}]
properties.name: Cassava

properties.summary: Dual-purpose cereal for food, poultry feed, and brewing across the Middle Belt and north.
properties.leadingNote: Kaduna and Benue are among the top maize states; the crop bridges Guinea savanna and forest-fringe rotations.
properties.sources: [{"label":"NAERLS — Maize production zones","url":"https://nfhl.naerls.gov.ng/index.php?solution_id=1000"}]
properties.name: Maize

properties.summary: Red palm oil and kernel oil from smallholder groves and estates in the humid south.
properties.leadingNote: South-south and south-east states anchor Nigeria's oil-palm belt; domestic refining of palm oil remains a major rural industry.
properties.sources: [{"label":"FAO — Oil palm development in Nigeria","url":"https://www.fao.org/4/ab592e/AB592E02.htm"}]
properties.name: Oil palm

properties.summary: Hevea plantations and smallholdings on the forest-savanna fringe and delta ridges.
properties.leadingNote: Edo and Delta host the largest mature rubber estates; Ondo and Cross River add substantial smallholder latex.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Rubber Research Institute of Nigeria (RRIN)","url":"https://rrin.gov.ng/"}]
properties.name: Rubber

properties.summary: Historic groundnut pyramid crop of the north-west and north-central savannas.
properties.leadingNote: Kano, Katsina, and Jigawa remain the core of Nigeria's groundnut belt — oil, cake, and kulikuli processing.
properties.sources: [{"label":"National Groundnut Producers, Processors and Marketers Association (NGPPMA)","url":"https://blueprint.ng/"}]
properties.name: Groundnut

properties.summary: Guinea corn staple and malt input across the Sudan and northern Guinea savannas.
properties.leadingNote: Northern states dominate sorghum for tuwo, pap, and brewery malt; Adamawa and Taraba extend production into the Middle Belt.
properties.sources: [{"label":"NAERLS — Sorghum production guide","url":"https://nfhl.naerls.gov.ng/"}]
properties.name: Sorghum

properties.summary: Early-maturing dryland cereal of the Sudan and Sahel savannas.
properties.leadingNote: Borno and Yobe lead millet output on the Lake Chad basin fringe; Jigawa and Kano are major suppliers to national markets.
properties.sources: [{"label":"FAO — Millet production in West Africa","url":"https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL"}]
properties.name: Millet

properties.summary: High-value oilseed export crop expanding across the north-east and north-west.
properties.leadingNote: Jigawa, Bauchi, and Gombe are frequently cited among Nigeria's top sesame exporters; Benue adds Middle Belt production.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Nigeria Export Promotion Council — Sesame seed profile","url":"https://nepc.gov.ng/"}]
properties.name: Sesame

properties.summary: Rain-fed lint crop of the northern Guinea and Sudan savannas for ginneries and textile mills.
properties.leadingNote: Kano and Kaduna anchor ginnery supply chains feeding Kaduna and Aba textile corridors.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Cotton Farmers Association of Nigeria (CFAN)","url":"https://guardian.ng/"}]
properties.name: Cotton

properties.summary: Export-oriented rhizome from the southern Kaduna highlands and Middle Belt.
properties.leadingNote: Southern Kaduna (Kachia, Kagarko) is Nigeria's best-known ginger cluster; Nasarawa and Benue add commercial volumes.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Nigeria Ginger Export Development Programme (media reports)","url":"https://guardian.ng/"}]
properties.name: Ginger

properties.summary: Irrigated dry-season tomatoes from Kadawa (Kano) and other northern fadama belts.
properties.leadingNote: Kadawa in Kano State is Nigeria's best-known tomato concentration; seasonal gluts and transport losses remain a policy focus.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Federal Ministry of Agriculture — Tomato value chain initiatives","url":"https://fmard.gov.ng/"}]
properties.name: Tomato

properties.summary: Staple cooking banana of the humid south and delta levees.
properties.leadingNote: Cross River and the south-south supply urban plantain markets year-round; intercropping under oil palm is common.
properties.sources: [{"label":"IITA — Plantain and banana systems in West Africa","url":"https://www.iita.org/"}]
properties.name: Plantain

properties.summary: Tree nut and apple crop expanding on Guinea savanna parklands.
properties.leadingNote: South-west states (Oyo, Osun, Ogun) lead raw cashew nut exports; processing hubs are growing around Ogbomoso and Ibadan.
properties.sources: [{"label":"National Cashew Association of Nigeria (NCAN)","url":"https://guardian.ng/"}]
properties.name: Cashew

properties.summary: Beans (dan wake) and leafy vegetable across the savanna — protein staple of the north.
properties.leadingNote: Borno and Yobe are major cowpea producers; Kano and Katsina supply national bean markets and da wake snacks.
properties.sources: [{"label":"IITA — Cowpea improvement programme","url":"https://www.iita.org/cowpea/"}]
properties.name: Cowpea

properties.summary: Oilseed and poultry-feed crop spreading through the Middle Belt and north.
properties.leadingNote: Benue and Niger are frequently cited among top soybean states, feeding poultry and oil mills in Lagos and the south-west.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Soybean Farmers Association of Nigeria (SOYAN)","url":"https://guardian.ng/"}]
properties.name: Soybean

properties.summary: Parkland shea butter tree across the Guinea savanna — women's cooperative processing.
properties.leadingNote: Guinea savanna states supply the bulk of Nigeria's shea kernels for butter and export; Niger and Kwara are major collection hubs.
properties.sources: [{"label":"Global Shea Alliance — Nigeria country profile","url":"https://www.globalshea.com/"}]
properties.name: Shea nut
